title: A quarter-second expiratory deceleration contrast does not improve cross-cycle wheeze prediction
abstract: In public NHANES adults, we tested 4*(2*FEV0.75-FEV0.5-FEV1)/FVC beyond flexible standard spirometric summaries and demographics. Source2007–08(n3667) grouped-CV Brier improved0.00003478, but target2011–12(n3644) Brier reduction was−0.00021541, approximate95% joint PSU-bootstrap interval[−0.00114282,+0.00009172]. Target AUC fell0.733984 to0.732254; log loss improved. Registered sensitivities and reverse transfer also had unfavorable Brier point estimates. This is an estimator- and scoring-rule-specific negative result, not equivalence or absence of physiology. Independent survey cycles share a platform and historical reuse; external clinical-cohort validation remains absent. Author AI self-checks and clean isolated reruns passed; no independent peer review claimed.
